problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{e}^{3t},\,{t}^{3}⟩.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$

feedback.problem:
The velocity vector $v=⟨u,v⟩$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
v=⟨{2}^{t},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1)⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the components of the acceleration vector $a$ at time $t.$

$a=⟨${{field-1}},{{field-2}}$⟩$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({2}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1))⟩ \\  & =⟨{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2,\,\frac{2t}{{t}^{2}+1}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
